llm_tab_desc: What actually happens when ChatGPT writes a sentence? Let's open the hood: how it reads your text, how it picks the next word, and why it costs money.
tok_desc: An LLM doesn't read words. It splits your text into chunks called tokens and turns each one into a number. Since the usage cost of these tools is calculated per token, not per word, this matters more than it sounds.
tok_input_placeholder: Type something to see how it is tokenized in real-time...
tok_g_legend: The Ġ prefix you may see is how BPE marks a leading space. It tells the model that Ġcat means " cat" (with the space), not just "cat".
dec_desc: An LLM doesn't "know" the next word. It computes a probability for thousands of possible words and picks one. Two knobs decide how it picks: Temperature (how bold) and Top-P (how strict).
dec_temp_desc: Low values (0.1) make the model boring and safe; it always picks the same top word. High values (1.5+) flatten the distribution so unusual words get a real chance.
dec_topp_desc: Keeps only the most probable words whose chances add up to P. The rest are crossed out, a guard against truly absurd choices, even when Temperature is high.

dt_visualize_tree_placeholder: Generate the Tree to visualize the graph.
dt_live_prediction_desc: Change feature values to see the decision path light up in real time.
dt_explain_what_is_body: Imagine you are deciding whether to take an umbrella. You ask yourself simple questions: 'Is it raining? Yes or No'. If it's not raining: 'Is it very windy?'. A Decision Tree is exactly that! The computer learns to create a sequence of easy questions to reach a final answer, just like a game of 20 Questions.
dt_explain_overfit_body: Imagine you have a math test tomorrow. You can either understand how the formulas work (Learn) or just memorize the exact questions and answers from a practice book (Memorize). If the teacher changes a single number on the real test, the one who memorized will fail, while the one who learned will pass! In Machine Learning, 'Overfitting' is when the computer just memorizes the data without understanding it.
dt_explain_pruning_body: If our question tree is huge and asks silly things like 'Does the person wear size 8 shoes?' or 'Did they eat an apple at 8 AM?', it becomes confusing and useless. Pruning is like trimming dry or useless branches from a garden bush. We remove unnecessary questions so the tree stays small, gets straight to the point, and is much better at guessing new situations.
dt_confirm_delete: Are you sure you want to delete this dataset?
dt_alert_min_rows: Please add at least 3 rows of data.
dt_err_json_must_be_array: The JSON file must be a list of objects.
dt_err_csv_min_rows: The CSV file must have at least a header line and one data row.
dt_err_min_samples: The dataset must have at least 3 samples.
dt_err_min_features: The dataset must have at least one feature and a target column.
dt_gini_desc: Measures class mixing in a group (purity). If a group is 100% pure (e.g., only 'Yes'), Gini is 0. The algorithm looks for splits that create the cleanest, most uniform groups possible.
dt_entropy_desc: Measures disorder or uncertainty (in bits). The algorithm picks the question that provides the highest 'Information Gain', maximizing the neatness and order of the resulting subsets.
dt_rule_path_none: No active rules (root node or no model).
dt_feature_importance_desc: Represents the mathematical contribution of each attribute to the reduction of impurity (Gini/Entropy) across tree splits, weighted by sample volume.
dt_code_exporter_desc: Use this self-contained, executable code to integrate this decision tree into other software environments.
onboarding_desc: Explore the inner workings of artificial intelligence through 100% visual, interactive labs running entirely in your browser.
onboarding_start_q: Would you like a quick interactive guided tour of the Computer Vision Lab?
tour_step1_desc: Track where you are: collect data, train, test, run diagnostics and finally the decision tree.
tour_step2_desc: Load a demo dataset (Animals or MNIST) to try it right away, or build your own project from scratch. Custom datasets are saved in your browser.
tour_step3_desc: Each card is a category to recognize. Click the name to rename it, and add or remove classes as needed (minimum of two).
tour_step4_desc: Feed each class with images from your webcam, by drawing freehand on the canvas, or by uploading files from your device.
tour_step5_desc: With at least two classes and some images, train here. Images pass through MobileNet v1 to extract features (embeddings) and the classifier is trained locally in seconds.
llm_tour_step1_desc: Switch between the Tokenizer, how text is split into tokens, and Decoding, where you see how the model picks the next word.
llm_tour_step2_desc: Compare simple word-level tokenization with subword (BPE) tokenization, the technique real models actually use.
llm_tour_step3_desc: Type any text here and watch it break into tokens in real time. Hover over a token to highlight it.
dt_tour_step1_desc: Pick a sample dataset (Golf or Iris) or import your own CSV/JSON file. The last column is treated as the target to predict.
dt_tour_step2_desc: Choose how the algorithm measures the 'purity' of each split: Gini or Entropy (information gain). The panel explains the difference and the tree recomputes instantly.
dt_tour_step3_desc: Control the tree's complexity before it grows: max depth, minimum samples to split, and minimum per leaf. Tighter limits help avoid overfitting.
dt_tour_step4_desc: Build the tree from the current data and parameters. It also recomputes automatically whenever you change a setting.
tour_step6_desc: Switch the test input between webcam, drawing or a file, to try the model on fresh images.
tour_step7_desc: The bars show the model's confidence for each class, live. After training, use 'Explain' to see a heatmap (XAI) revealing which areas of the image drove the decision.
tour_step8_desc: Add test images and evaluate the model: the confusion matrix crosses the true label with the predicted one, plus per-class precision, recall and F1. Click a cell to inspect the samples behind it.
tour_step9_desc: Finally, build a decision tree over the embeddings, an interpretable, complementary view of how the model separates the classes.
llm_tour_step4_desc: The number of tokens drives the cost of using a model. Here you see your text's token count and an associated cost estimate.
llm_tour_step5_desc: Temperature controls creativity: low values make the model more predictable and focused; high values flatten the distribution and produce more varied, riskier outputs.
llm_tour_step6_desc: Top-p keeps only the most likely words whose cumulative probability reaches the threshold P, discarding the long tail of unlikely options.
llm_tour_step7_desc: Combining temperature and Top-p, this is the final distribution and the most likely word to be picked. Adjust the parameters and watch the result change.
dt_tour_step5_desc: Compare training accuracy with test accuracy. A large gap signals overfitting, when the tree memorizes the data instead of learning general rules.
dt_tour_step6_desc: View the tree as a graph, read the rules as IF/ELSE text, or export the model as Python/JavaScript code. You can also apply post-pruning to simplify the tree.
dt_tour_step7_desc: Fill in the feature values and watch the prediction update in real time, with the decision path lighting up on the tree.
